newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: SE Asian Grain - Malaysia buys wheat, trade quiet.
newsitem.headline: SE Asian Grain - Malaysia buys wheat, trade quiet.

text.p: Malaysia was said to have bought 25,000 tonnes of Argentine wheat recently, but otherwise the regional grains and oilseeds business in Southeast Asia remained mostly quiet, traders said on Wednesday.
The Argentine wheat was for December/January shipment and was bought at US$173-$175 a tonne C&F, Malaysian dealers said.
"We heard this was done, but it's hard confirming who the buyer was," said a trader in Kuala Lumpur. "Otherwise, there's been little activity this week."

The only other deal being talked about was that Thailand is close to clinching agreement to buy 25,000 tonnes of soymeal and 15,000 tonnes of soybeans from the United States for October shipment, Thai traders said.
"I hope the deal can be concluded," one commented.
They said Thai industry buyers were likely to purchase more soymeal soon on concerns that world oilseed prices could rise further if an early frost hits U.S. soybean crop areas.

The Thai feedmill industry, meanwhile, will have to wait for the resignation of Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa before a proposal to trim import duties to help the meat and poultry industries could be considered anew by the next government.

The Commerce Ministry proposed cutting duties to 10 percent from 15 percent for soymeal, to zero for soybeans and corn/maize from the previous five and three percent, and to 15 percent -- plus a 140 baht/tonne surcharge -- from six percent plus a 1,400 baht/tonne surcharge for fishmeal.
The domestic price paid for benchmark 14.5 percent-moisture maize paid by feed producers was quoted around 4.30-4.50 baht a kg compared with 4.50-4.60 baht a kg last week, dealers said.

"The supply was low but so was demand. It seemed like buyers were sidelined to wait for the second crop, which will start entering the market by the end of next month," said a source from the Thai Maize and Produce Traders Association.
Tight supply pushed prices of soymeal up to 10.30-10.40 baht a kg from 10.20 baht last week.
Fresh imported soymeal supply was not expected to be available until next month, industry and official sources said.
But supply shortages were partly alleviated by easier prices of fishmeal which could be used as a substitute for soymeal, they added.
In Malaysia, traders said "A" grade wheat in bags was quoted at 840 ringgit a tonne ex-factory/godown central region from 880 ringgit in the previous week.
Low-grade wheat was steady at 550-600 ringgit.
Local soymeal was at 818.46 ringgit a tonne from 801.92 ringgit last week. Imported soymeal was going for about 780-800 ringgit a tonne from the previous range of 760-780 ringgit.
Bulk corn prices were stable at 550 ringgit ex-factory/godown in the central region.
In Indonesia, corn prices stayed soft with supplies ample due to the recent harvest and weak demand, traders said.
High quality full yellow corn with a maximum of 16 percent water content was on offer at 420 rupiah a kg in Lampung compared with 455-460 rupiah in mid-September, they said.
"Corn demand is likely to remain weak due to falling chicken egg prices which have a negative impact on poultry breeders," one trader in Jakarta said.
He said egg prices had dropped to around 1,800 rupiah/kg currently from the usual 2,400 rupiah/kg.
Another dealer said the recent harvest in Lampung, which produces around 200,000 tonnes of corn a year, was still largely in the warehouses of some big feedmillers.
Indonesian soymeal prices stayed firm. Soymeal was traded at 820-830 rupiah a kg in Jakarta, traders said.
